SchemaBot is the system that knows what is in your databases. This guide is
for building a service on that knowledge: a schema inventory that pulls live
schemas, a dashboard that polls apply status, an agentic tool that queries
schema information across your fleet, a replication control plane that needs
to know which tables exist and when they changed.

Everything a consumer needs sits on the read tier, so a service can be built
without any write access. How a service authenticates (and why service callers
are read-only by design) is covered in
[calling SchemaBot as a service](auth.md#calling-schemabot-as-a-service); this
guide covers the endpoints themselves.

## The four core endpoints

| Endpoint | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/databases` | Every registered database, with type and environments |
| `POST /api/pull` | A live schema snapshot of one database |
| `GET /api/history/{database}` | Every apply for a database, with states and timestamps |
| `GET /api/progress/apply/{apply_id}` | Per-table detail for one apply: the DDL, change type, and progress |

The expected call pattern is periodic sync: `databases` discovers the fleet,
recurring `pull` calls snapshot the schemas the service cares about, and
`history` and `progress` answer what changed and when. All timestamps are UTC
in RFC 3339 format.

## Listing databases

`GET /api/databases` enumerates every database registered with the deployment.
It is the natural sync root: discover the fleet here, then fan out `pull`
calls from the result.

```json
{
  "databases": [
    {
      "database": "payments",
      "type": "mysql",
      "environments": [
        { "environment": "staging" },
        { "environment": "production" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "database": "orders",
      "type": "vitess",
      "environments": [
        { "environment": "production", "deployments": ["orders-primary"] }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

An environment may also list `deployments`, the execution targets that carry
out schema changes for it. That is a routing detail most consumers can ignore:
`database` plus `environment` is the address every other endpoint takes.

## Pulling a schema

`POST /api/pull` returns a live snapshot of one database in one environment,
read from the database itself rather than from the schema repository. This is
the source of truth for "what is actually deployed right now".

```json
{
  "database": "payments",
  "environment": "production",
  "type": "mysql",
  "catalog_detail": "basic"
}
```

`catalog_detail` selects the response shape. `basic` (the default) returns
each table's full `SHOW CREATE TABLE` DDL:

```json
{
  "database": "payments",
  "type": "mysql",
  "environment": "production",
  "table_count": 2,
  "namespaces": {
    "payments": {
      "tables": {
        "accounts": "CREATE TABLE `accounts` (\n  `id` bigint unsigned NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,\n  ...",
        "ledger_entries": "CREATE TABLE `ledger_entries` (\n  `id` bigint unsigned NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,\n  ..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The response is grouped by namespace (the database name for MySQL, the
keyspace for Vitess), so a sharded Vitess database and a plain MySQL database
come back in the same shape.

`catalog_detail: detailed` adds structured metadata alongside the DDL: a
`namespace_catalog` summary per namespace and a `table_catalog` entry per
table with columns, indexes, and engine-maintained size estimates.

```json
"namespaces": {
  "payments": {
    "tables": { "accounts": "CREATE TABLE `accounts` ( ... )" },
    "namespace_catalog": { "name": "payments", "engine": "mysql", "table_count": 2 },
    "table_catalog": {
      "accounts": {
        "name": "accounts",
        "kind": "table",
        "columns": [
          { "name": "id", "type": "bigint unsigned", "nullable": false, "auto_increment": true },
          { "name": "balance_cents", "type": "bigint", "nullable": false }
        ],
        "indexes": [
          { "name": "PRIMARY", "primary": true, "unique": true, "parts": ["id"] }
        ],
        "estimated_row_count": 1204833,
        "data_size_bytes": 287309824
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`estimated_row_count` and `data_size_bytes` are engine-maintained estimates,
not exact counts. Catalog depth also varies by engine: MySQL returns the full
per-table catalog, while Vitess currently returns the namespace-level summary
only. The DDL in `tables` is complete on every engine, so a consumer that
parses DDL is never short-changed.

## Apply history

`GET /api/history/{database}` lists every apply for a database, newest first.
Filter to one environment with `?environment=production`.

```json
{
  "database": "payments",
  "applies": [
    {
      "apply_id": "apply-3f9c2ab8e1d04b7a",
      "caller": "myorg/payments-service#412",
      "engine": "spirit",
      "environment": "production",
      "state": "completed",
      "started_at": "2026-08-12T14:30:05Z",
      "completed_at": "2026-08-12T14:41:52Z"
    },
    {
      "apply_id": "apply-9d41c07be2a8f356",
      "caller": "cli",
      "engine": "spirit",
      "environment": "staging",
      "state": "failed",
      "error": "schema change failed; see server logs",
      "error_code": "engine_error",
      "started_at": "2026-08-11T09:12:44Z",
      "completed_at": "2026-08-11T09:13:01Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

`caller` tells you where the apply came from: `repo#PR` for the PR workflow,
`cli` for the Admin CLI. `state` values are the apply states from the
[state machine](architecture.md#state-machine); `completed`, `failed`,
`stopped`, and `cancelled` are the terminal ones a history consumer usually
cares about.

## Apply progress

`GET /api/progress/apply/{apply_id}` gives per-table detail for one apply: the
DDL that ran, the change type, row-copy progress while it is running, and
timestamps once it is done. Poll it for applies that `history` reports as
still active, or to answer "what exactly did that apply change".

```json
{
  "apply_id": "apply-3f9c2ab8e1d04b7a",
  "state": "running",
  "engine": "spirit",
  "database": "payments",
  "environment": "production",
  "caller": "myorg/payments-service#412",
  "pull_request": "https://github.com/myorg/payments-service/pull/412",
  "started_at": "2026-08-12T14:30:05Z",
  "summary": "Running: copying rows (64%)",
  "volume": 5,
  "tables": [
    {
      "table_name": "accounts",
      "ddl": "ALTER TABLE `accounts` ADD COLUMN `closed_at` timestamp NULL",
      "change_type": "alter",
      "status": "running",
      "rows_copied": 771093,
      "rows_total": 1204833,
      "percent_complete": 64,
      "eta_seconds": 240,
      "started_at": "2026-08-12T14:30:06Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

`summary` is a human-readable status line for display; parse the structured
fields, not the summary. Vitess applies additionally carry per-shard progress
under each table's `shards` list, in the same rows-copied shape.

## The write tier

The same API also carries the endpoints that change things: `POST /api/plan`,
`POST /api/apply`, the control operations, and lock acquisition. Those sit on
the write tier, and their intended callers are the
[PR workflow and the Admin CLI](architecture.md#user-layer-cli--pr-comments--api),
which layer locking, review gates, and progress reporting on top. A service
consumer does not get and does not need that tier:
[the auth model](auth.md#the-two-tier-api-model) explains the split, and no
configuration grants a service the write tier.
